name: Fix a kubelet that won't start
objective: CKA › Cluster Architecture, Maintenance & Troubleshooting. A worker's kubelet won't start, so the node is NotReady and kubectl can't help you on the node itself. Diagnose it the way the exam expects — systemctl status kubelet, journalctl -u kubelet, systemctl cat kubelet to find the offending drop-in — then fix it and bring the node back Ready. Graded on persistent node state via docker exec and kubectl -o json.

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a worker kubelet that won't start
questions.teach:
The **kubelet** is the node agent: it runs as a systemd service (`kubelet.service`), reads its config from `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml`, and takes extra settings from drop-ins under `/etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/`. When it won't start, that node goes **NotReady** — and because the break is *on the node*, `kubectl` can't tell you why. You diagnose from the node with **systemd + journald**.

**Gotcha:** `systemctl status kubelet` shows it failed; `systemctl cat kubelet` prints the unit **plus every drop-in** so you can spot a bad one; `journalctl -u kubelet -e --no-pager` shows the real error. After changing a **unit or drop-in** you must `systemctl daemon-reload` *before* `systemctl restart kubelet` (a `config.yaml` edit needs only the restart).
questions.prompt:
Setup installed a broken systemd **drop-in** for the kubelet on `$W2`, so the kubelet won't start and `$W2` is `NotReady`. Diagnose it on the node and bring the kubelet back.

Target: node `$W2` is `Ready` again and the broken drop-in under `/etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/` is gone.
questions.hint: Confirm the damage: `kubectl get nodes` shows `$W2` NotReady. Shell in: `docker exec -it $W2 bash`. `systemctl status kubelet` → failed (a failing `ExecStartPre`). `systemctl cat kubelet` reveals the offending file under `/etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/` (name has `lab-break`). Remove it, then `systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart kubelet`; `journalctl -u kubelet -e --no-pager | tail` should now show a clean start. Give the node ~30s to report Ready.
questions.solution:
# confirm from base: W2 is NotReady
kubectl get nodes

# shell onto the broken worker (exam equivalent: ssh $W2)
docker exec -it $W2 bash

# why won't kubelet start?
systemctl status kubelet                 # failed: ExecStartPre=/bin/false exited 1
systemctl cat kubelet                    # unit + drop-ins; spot 99-lab-break.conf
journalctl -u kubelet -e --no-pager | tail

# remove the bad drop-in and reload systemd, then restart kubelet
rm -f /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/99-lab-break.conf
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl restart kubelet
systemctl status kubelet                 # active (running)
exit

# back on base: W2 returns Ready in ~30s
kubectl get node $W2 -w

verification.description: Broken kubelet drop-in removed on $W2 and the node is Ready again

questions.eli5:
Every worker node has a hard-working foreman called the **kubelet**. It's the one employee on the node who actually talks to the cluster boss (the API server), starts the containers, and reports "I'm alive and healthy." If the foreman doesn't clock in, the whole node is considered absent — Kubernetes marks it **NotReady** and schedules nothing there.

Here's the catch: because the foreman is the node's *only* link to the boss, when he's not working you **can't ask him anything through `kubectl`**. You have to walk onto the node and ask the building's own systems directly. The kubelet is run by **systemd** (the node's startup manager), so systemd knows exactly why it won't start.

The foreman reads his instructions from a few places. The main contract is `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml`, but systemd also stacks on **drop-in** notes from `/etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/`. Someone slipped a bad drop-in in there (a note like "before you start, run this command that always fails"). So the foreman tries, fails the pre-check, and gives up every time.

You find it, delete it, tell systemd "re-read your notes," and restart the kubelet.

**Watch out:**

- `kubectl` is useless for the diagnosis — the break is *on the node*. Use `systemctl status kubelet`, `systemctl cat kubelet`, and `journalctl -u kubelet`.
- `systemctl cat kubelet` prints the unit **plus every drop-in** — that's how you spot the bad `.conf` file.
- After changing a **unit or drop-in**, you **must** run `systemctl daemon-reload` *before* `systemctl restart kubelet`. (A plain `config.yaml` edit only needs the restart.)
- Give the node ~30 seconds to flip back to **Ready** after the restart.
questions.deepDive:
## Diagnosing a kubelet that won't start — full rundown

### Mental model
The **kubelet** is the per-node agent. It registers the node with the API server, runs static pods and scheduled pods, and reports node status (`Ready`/`NotReady`). It runs as a **systemd service** (`kubelet.service`), not as a pod — so when it's down, `kubectl` cannot help you diagnose it. You troubleshoot **on the node** with `systemd` + `journald`.

### Where the kubelet gets its configuration
| Source | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Systemd unit | `/usr/lib/systemd/system/kubelet.service` (or `/etc/systemd/system/...`) | base service definition |
| Drop-ins | `/etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/*.conf` | override/append flags (kubeadm puts `10-kubeadm.conf` here) |
| Kubelet config | `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` | `KubeletConfiguration` (cgroupDriver, clusterDNS, auth, etc.) |
| Env file | `/var/lib/kubelet/kubeadm-flags.env` | `KUBELET_KUBEADM_ARGS` |
| Kubeconfig | `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf` | how kubelet talks to the apiserver |

Drop-ins are read **in lexical order**; later files override earlier ones. A bad `99-*.conf` therefore wins.

### Diagnose (on the node)
```bash
docker exec -it $W2 bash            # exam: ssh $W2

systemctl status kubelet           # active? failed? what was the last error line?
systemctl cat kubelet              # prints the unit + EVERY drop-in -> spot the bad one
journalctl -u kubelet -e --no-pager | tail   # the real error from the last start attempt
journalctl -u kubelet -f           # follow live while you restart
```
Typical failures:
| Status / journal line | Cause |
|---|---|
| `ExecStartPre=/bin/false (code=exited, status=1)` | a drop-in added a pre-start that always fails |
| `unknown flag` / `failed to parse` | bad flag in a drop-in or env file |
| `misconfiguration: kubelet cgroup driver ... does not match` | cgroupDriver mismatch in `config.yaml` |
| `no such file or directory` for config | wrong `--config` path |

### Fix and restart (the critical order)
```bash
rm -f /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/99-lab-break.conf   # remove the bad drop-in

systemctl daemon-reload            # REQUIRED after any unit/drop-in change
systemctl restart kubelet
systemctl status kubelet           # active (running)
exit
kubectl get node $W2 -w            # Ready in ~30s
```

### When do you need daemon-reload?
| What you changed | daemon-reload? | restart kubelet? |
|---|---|---|
| A systemd **unit** or **drop-in** (`*.service`, `*.conf`) | ✅ yes | ✅ yes |
| `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` | ❌ no | ✅ yes |
| `kubeadm-flags.env` | ❌ no | ✅ yes |

`daemon-reload` makes systemd re-read unit files; it does **not** restart the service — you still restart kubelet separately.

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **`kubectl` can't diagnose a dead kubelet** — the node has no agent to answer. Always go to the node.
- **Forgetting `daemon-reload`** after editing a unit/drop-in: systemd keeps the old (broken) definition and your restart changes nothing.
- `systemctl cat kubelet` is the fastest way to *see every active override in one screen* — use it to find the rogue drop-in instead of guessing filenames.
- Use `journalctl -u kubelet -e` (jump to end) or `--since "-5min"` to read the latest attempt; don't scroll the whole history.
- The node may take ~20–40s to flip to `Ready` after a healthy kubelet start — don't assume failure immediately.
- Don't delete `10-kubeadm.conf` — that's the legitimate kubeadm drop-in; remove only the injected/broken file.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl get nodes                                  # $W2 NotReady
docker exec -it $W2 bash                           # ssh $W2 in the exam
systemctl status kubelet                           # failed + reason
systemctl cat kubelet                              # find the bad drop-in
journalctl -u kubelet -e --no-pager | tail         # exact error
rm -f /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/99-lab-break.conf
systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart kubelet
kubectl get node $W2 -w                            # back to Ready
```
